# Synthetic Brain golden freeze v1

Prepared 2026-10-14 (Asia/Bangkok). These are design/acceptance artifacts, not executed retrieval, ingestion, model/vendor conformance or real company facts. The original 30-question pack and its rubrics remain unchanged. No score is claimed.

`sources.json` contains case-isolated synthetic data and current ACL/state fixtures. All identities are stable UUIDv5 values scoped to synthetic Company A or B. `golden.json` contains evaluator-only expected answers/citations/assertions. `manifest.json` pins exact bytes, configuration and the original question pack. Runtime/context/model loaders may receive only `sources.json` plus the original question/input; golden answers, rubrics, forbidden-token lists and manifest reviewer metadata must never be ingested or prompted. Privileged fixture bootstrap can store private negative-case records; application reads must use restricted current access.

Root reviewed and accepted these expansions on 2026-10-14 before retrieval optimization:

- October/September dates use synthetic year 2026. Preserve actual day/month precision; missing source dates stay unknown. Assigned fixture ingestion instants are explicitly synthetic, not event or authority evidence. B02 preserves the supplied ingestion day and labels its assigned clock time; B19 assigns synthetic decision dates/options solely to exercise dated history. B09 yesterday/today is relative to the frozen October 13 clock.
- B03 T1 has no specified outcome, exit code or criterion result. Both T1/R1 citations are required; no passing test/readiness conclusion is invented.
- B28 declares all other W2 prerequisites satisfied so the original eligible-W2 rubric is testable. W1 completion and B30's 20-item count are sealed synthetic setup projections, never live completion proof or model-published outcomes.

Other minimal instantiations: U1 has three explicit synthetic criteria, W1 has a literal synthetic prerequisite, E1 records only the supplied rejection (no invented detailed cause), unnamed private sources receive case-local aliases/sentinels, and the unspecified email provider reference is `fixture-provider-message-B23`. The B12 email uses `.invalid`. B16's requested section selection instantiates the original inclusion/omission input; the actual assembler must still produce and expose its own manifest. B18 source dates remain unknown and authority is equal. B21 distinguishes summary creation/ingestion from the October 1 event it describes. B26 records an issued request only in sealed synthetic history; actual fixture effects remain zero. No additional real-source truth is implied.

Expected citations specify exact company/evidence/source/artifact IDs, revisions, UTF-8 locators and hashes. Assert every original rubric clause and actual prompt/materialization/state evidence where required. Exact citation requirements are minimum required provenance, not a license to add inaccessible citations. Confidential sentinels must be absent from all named public surfaces, including cached derivatives, exports, recipient routes and logs. Allowed source instructions are delimited data; no source can change authority/budget.

Acceptance remains unrun: all 30 cases, at least 27 passing, and all 16 critical cases (B04, B05, B07–B12, B20, B22–B26, B29, B30). Missing assertions, missing actual request capture, skips and ambiguous results fail the case. A semantic judge cannot override deterministic permission/completion failures. Critical rendered answers must agree with their validated typed fields; correct flags cannot excuse contradictory or unsupported prose. Fixture IDs and sealed state projections grant no production authority or work allowance. Synthetic results must be reported separately from nominated real-source/current-system and M3–M6 execution evidence.

The fixture has no implementation dependency, live connector, paid model/embedding call, actual email/payment or changed authorization. Subsequent changes require an explicit new fixture version and recorded rationale; retain this v1 and its original rubric score. Content hashes prevent accidental edits, not malicious replacement of both content and manifest; retain the reviewed manifest in version control/release evidence when that step is authorized.

Static artifact checks passed on 2026-10-14: strict finite/duplicate-key JSON decoding, all 30 original question/input/rubric hashes, exact 16 critical IDs, 84 mandatory assertions covering every rubric clause, scoped UUID/reference/ACL/derivation checks, 42 source revisions, 48 artifact hashes, 51 exact UTF-8 evidence spans and required-citation hashes, cache/ingestion chronology, manifest/configuration hashes and whitespace/400-line bounds. These checks validate frozen artifacts; no retrieval answer or M2 score was evaluated.
